title: Signal Compactification and Operator Playbook
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
A compact operator workflow to reduce metric cardinality, keep dashboards actionable, and ensure traces carry minimal but sufficient context for fast investigation. Focus is on cheap signal (low-cardinality aggregates + flags) + targeted high-fidelity traces for high-severity incidents. This is a pragmatic companion to full instrumentation planning — assumed to be used in live incidents, runbooks, and quarterly hygiene sprints.

Why now:
- Query costs rising as more per-tenant and per-model labels are added to metrics.
- Operators overwhelmed by noisy dashboards (too many series) during token-surge incidents.
- We need a reproducible minimal set of signals that map to rapid hypotheses (cold cache, KV key miss, batching stalled, model fallback).

Key principles (short):
- Favor aggregates that answer operator questions in < 60s.
- Move dimension complexity to debugging-only traces, not 1-minute dashboards.
- Add boolean trace annotations for binary hypotheses (cold_start=true) so sampling is targeted.
- Use adaptive sampling to protect trace budget when spike detection triggers.

Compact metric set (starter):
- inference.requests.count (global, per-region) — integer
- inference.tokens.generated.p50/p90/p99 (global) — latencies per-token
- inference.kv.cache.hit_rate (global, tenant-agg) — ratio
- runtime.batch.size.mean (global) — mean batch size distribution
- routing.fallback.rate (global) — percent requests routed to cheaper/older model
- capacity.utilization.gpu_pct (pool) — 0-100 integer
- operator.signal.noise_index (global) — derived score for dashboard noise
Notes: keep cardinality to region/pool/host where helpful; avoid tenant unless critical — use tenant-rollups instead.

Compact dashboard layout (micro-panels, order):
1) Availability ribbon (error rate, 5m moving percent; local to region)
2) Latency slices (p50/p95/p99 token latency; stacked per latency bucket)
3) Cost/throughput lens (tokens/s, batch size mean, requests/s)
4) Cache health (kv hit rate, cold_start boolean rate)
5) Fallbacks & throttles (routing.fallback.rate, rate_limit.errors)
6) Operator noise index and recent alert list
Design notes: each panel should render under 300ms for the standard time range and not exceed 4 series by default. Expanders can show per-pool breakdown.

Tracing conventions (minimal tags and boolean annotations):
- trace.tag:hook = runtime|router|cache|kv|model
- trace.tag:tenant_bucket = small|medium|large (computed at ingest)
- trace.annotation:cold_start = true|false (boolean flag set at first model load attempt)
- trace.annotation:kv_miss = true|false
- trace.annotation:batch_wait_ms = <int> (only for traces sampled for slow-path)
Guidelines: store boolean annotations as explicit indexed fields to enable fast search for ‘cold_start=true’ across sample corpus. Avoid adding freeform prompt contents to traces; redact full inputs.

Adaptive sampling & budget rules:
- Default trace sample rate: 0.1% of requests.
- Spike mode: when operator.noise_index > threshold or requests/s > 2x baseline, increase sample rate to 2% for 10 minutes for traces tagged router|cache.
- High-severity mode: if SLO breach persists >5m, sample all traces for requests hitting fallback routes for 30m.
Rationale: target samples where hypothesis resolution is fastest (router/cache) rather than across-the-board increase.

Operator checklist (incident first 15 minutes):
- Step 0: Confirm symptom: is user-visible latency or error spike? Use availability ribbon.
- Step 1: Check latency slices + token generation p99; is latency token-path or pre-token (router/cache)?
- Step 2: Toggle spike-mode sampling if the noise index indicates insufficient traces.
- Step 3: Query for traces with annotation cold_start=true and kv_miss=true (use boolean filters).
- Step 4: If cache miss high and batch size low, suspect cold-cache / warmup; consider warmup job or increase prefix caching TTLs.
- Step 5: If fallback.rate elevated without capacity utilization spike, suspect policy/regression — escalate to routing owner.
- Step 6: Document initial hypothesis in incident ticket (Jira template linked) and mark which boolean annotations were decisive.

Mini runbook queries (examples):
- kv miss rate over 5m: sum(rate(inference_kv_miss_total[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m]))
- cold_start traces last 30m (sampled): traces("annotation.cold_start=true") | sort timestamp desc | head 50
- batch size median: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(runtime_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le))
Note: these are example PromQL/trace search snippets — adapt to the tenant-rollup conventions.

Dashboard hygiene sprint items (quarterly checklist):
- Remove panels with >20% of queries using high-cardinality labels; convert to rollup metrics.
- Audit all panels with tenant labels — add rollup alternatives and limit default time ranges to 1h.
- Confirm boolean trace annotations are indexed in trace store.
- Add noise index badge to the team on-call dashboard.

Metric ownership mapping (who to call quickly):
- routing.fallback.rate -> eng-serving-runtime (oncall routing)
- kv.cache.hit_rate -> eng-serving-runtime / cache owner
- batch.size.* -> serving-runtime / scheduler
- capacity.utilization.gpu_pct -> infra / capacity-planning
Add phone-home alias lists in Confluence page OBS-ops-oncall.

Open questions & tradeoffs (short):
- How much tenant granularity do we accept in dashboards before query costs dominate? (proposal: tenant rollups only for top-50 tenants by token volume).
- Do boolean annotations add too much index pressure? We need benchmarks on trace-store indexing cost.
- Where to store operator.noise_index algorithm — alerts or metric? current plan: export as metric so dashboards can plot it cheaply.

Next steps (owners & dates):
- Build boolean trace annotation proof-of-concept (Avery) — target 2024-11-30
- Pilot adaptive sampling rules in staging with two regions (Maya) — target 2024-12-15
- Dashboard slimming pass: remove 10 high-cardinality panels (Kai) — target 2025-01-15
- Cost estimation for trace boolean indexing (Lina + infra) — target 2024-12-01

Notes to self / informal bits:
- Keep a ready-to-run synthetic probe that toggles cold_start=true for warmup tests.
- We should avoid per-tenant timeseries on default dashboards — they are the biggest signal of chaos.
- This doc is intentionally compact; will expand with queries and Grafana panel JSON once sprint resources allocated.

Appendix: quick glossary (one-liners)
- Compactification: reducing metric surface area while preserving operator value.
- Boolean trace annotation: indexed true/false flags in traces for rapid filtering.
- Noise index: heuristic combining rare-series-rate + alert-churn to flag dashboard overload.

End of doc.
